name: CA-26
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+9 partisan lean favors the Democratic nominee in an open seat
Jacqui Irwin holds a large money advantage: about $1.1M raised and $447K on hand versus Sam Gallucci's $29K in cash
Prediction markets price the Democratic nominee near 96 percent
Open-seat dynamic and absence of polling add uncertainty
model.rationale: The district's nine-point Democratic lean, Irwin's roughly two-to-one fundraising edge and outside backing, and markets pricing her near certain outweigh the uncertainty of an open seat with no available polling.
model.watch: Heavy late Republican outside spending or a sharply nationalized environment could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Julia Brownley (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
California's 26th District leans Democratic by nine points, and Julia Brownley's retirement places an open seat on the ballot. State Assemblymember Jacqui Irwin carries the Democratic banner with a substantial financial edge: she has raised about $1.1 million and holds $447,000 on hand, supplemented by roughly $366,000 in outside support. Republican Sam Gallucci has raised about $489,000 but reports just $29,000 in cash, with no outside spending recorded on either side.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available, so the outlook rests on the district's partisan lean, the money gap, and prediction markets, which price the Democratic nominee near 96 percent. The open-seat dynamic removes the incumbent's usual advantage and adds some uncertainty, but the combination of district geography and resource disparities keeps the seat firmly in the Democratic column this cycle.
